children.name: Prompt Architecture and Style Replication
children.blurb: Prompt architecture and style replication concerns how artists and illustrators structure text prompts to direct generative image models toward a desired visual outcome, including the deliberate imitation of an existing artist's or period's style.

sections.body: Visual arts and generative illustration covers still images made with diffusion models. It includes prompt architecture, concept art, vector assets, inpainting, and colour grading. Artificial intelligence is actually doing these tasks now through text-to-image systems that turn written descriptions into raster images, and through editing tools that fill missing areas or shift colour palettes. The work is practical, not theoretical: artists and designers use these systems to produce concept sketches, interface elements, and finished illustrations. The section focuses on the still image, not video or audio.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The site currently tracks zero live image generation models and zero AI tools, so the state of the field here is described through techniques rather than named products. Some tasks are solved well enough for daily use, such as generating a plausible image from a short prompt and extending a canvas with matching content. Other tasks remain limited, including exact style replication, consistent vector output, and colour grading that matches a specific brand or film look. Honest limits include unpredictable details, difficulty controlling fine geometry, and the need for manual cleanup. The absence of tracked models means the reader will not find performance comparisons or version histories.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages move from the words that drive an image to the final colour adjustments. Prompt Architecture and Style Replication explains how to structure text and reference images to get a desired look. Concept Art and World-Building shows how those prompts become environments, characters, and props for pre-production. Vector Graphics and Interface Assets covers the harder problem of turning diffusion output into clean, scalable shapes for apps and print. Inpainting and Canvas Expansion deals with fixing parts of an image or extending its borders after the first generation. Algorithmic Colour Grading closes the loop by adjusting hue, saturation, and tone across a finished still.
